chunks: Ismail ibn Muslim narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a woman who asked him: 'I have a husband who is harsh with me, and I made something to make him more affectionate toward me.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'Woe to you! You have polluted the seas, corrupted the earth, and the righteous angels and the angels of the heavens and the earth have cursed you.' The woman then fasted during the day, prayed during the night, shaved her head, and wore rough clothing. When this was reported to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said: 'None of this will be accepted from her.'

key_terms.الْبِحَارَ: The seas (metaphor for depth of impurity)
key_terms.الْمُسُوحَ: Rough woolen garments worn by penitents

ai.seo_question: Why was the woman's repentance not accepted after she practiced magic on her husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights the specific gravity of *sihr* (magic) in marital relations, where the Prophet (SAW) curses the woman for 'muddying the seas and the clay,' a metaphor for corrupting the fundamental elements of creation. Notably, despite her rigorous ascetic repentance—fasting, night prayer, and wearing *musuh* (rough wool)—the Prophet declared her repentance 'not accepted,' a point of scholarly debate regarding whether this refers to the specific act of magic or a unique divine decree for this case. This narrative underscores the distinct status of magic as a major sin that may require a specific expiation beyond general acts of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4544 - Ismail ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) and said: "I have a husband who is harsh with me, and I made something (a charm or spell) to make him more affectionate toward me."
The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said to her: "Woe to you! You have polluted the seas, corrupted the earth, and the righteous angels and the angels of the heavens and the earth have cursed you."
The woman then fasted during the day, prayed during the night, shaved her head, and wore rough clothing as an act of repentance. When this was reported to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), he said: "None of this will be accepted from her."
